record.body:
## Rationale

aff check and aff close-batch run a command and copy its exit into workflow records; outside orchestra that is a thin wrapper over a test runner. The part that answers a question no runner answers is already here: aff verdict reads a committed claims manifest and asks whether a frozen test fails at base on an assertion and passes at head. The hunk-revert, llm-mutants, and differential spikes add the other two questions: which changed code no test notices, and which behavior changed that no claim asked for. Together they audit one change from git alone, so any agent workflow, a human pull request, or CI can use it.

## Counter-argument

Only protecting the tests (manifest, frozen hashes, signed amendments, verdict) is smaller, already mostly built, and has no LLM or multi-runner cost. Mutation and differential testing exist as tools (mutmut, Stryker), so the audit's novelty is the combination around claims, not any one technique, and support for runners other than pytest is real work.

payload.alternatives: only protect the tests (manifest, hashes, amendments, verdict); a broader QA agent that writes and explores tests
payload.choice: affidavit audits a code change from git: claims with a frozen witness, changed code no test notices, behavior changes no claim asked for; CLI plus CI check

record.subject: affidavit-product
